reviews.name: Met office reviewer
reviews.summary: The only verified input is an internal no-notice drill message bracketed by 'Exercise, Exercise, Exercise'. The alert instead tells the public that a ballistic missile is inbound, with status Actual, certainty Observed and severity Extreme, and it says 'THIS IS NOT A DRILL'. No verified hazard supports any of these fields. Issuing this would be a false public missile alert, the January 2018 Hawaii failure mode. A person must stop this message and decide whether anything should go out at all.

objections.issue: The hazard is not supported by any verified input. The only verified source describes an internal drill message, not an observed or forecast missile threat. The headline and description assert a real inbound ballistic missile.
objections.fix: Do not issue a public missile warning. A responsible official must confirm whether any real hazard exists. If it does not, this message must not be sent to the public.

reviews.name: Met office reviewer
reviews.summary: The alert does not match the verified input on place or hazard. It says 'in your area' instead of naming Calabasas, Agoura Hills and West Hills, and it never names the Kenneth Fire or says the hazard is a wildfire. The drafter can fix both. Severity (Severe), urgency (Expected) and certainty (Likely) are consistent with an evacuation warning.

objections.issue: The alert does not name the affected places. The verified input limits the warning to people near Calabasas, Agoura Hills and the West Hills community in the western San Fernando Valley. The alert only says 'in your area', and anyone outside the fire area who receives it, for example on a phone with imprecise geotargeting, cannot tell they are not affected.
objections.fix: Replace 'has been issued in your area' with the named locations, e.g. 'An EVACUATION WARNING has been issued for areas near Calabasas, Agoura Hills and the West Hills community in the western San Fernando Valley.' Add the place names to the headline as well.

reviews.name: Network operator and regulator reviewer
reviews.summary: The English text (317 GSM-7 characters, 4 pages) is deliverable and the page count is correct at 93 characters per page. However, page 1 does not carry the hazard and the action. The first 93 characters are mostly preamble ("NEW: This is an emergency message from the Los Angeles County Fire Department.") and end mid-phrase at "An EVACUATION". The action ("be ready to evacuate") only appears on page 2. The drafter can fix this by reordering the text.

objections.issue: Page 1 lacks the hazard and the action. At 93 GSM-7 characters per page, page 1 holds only the "NEW:" tag, the sender preamble and the cut-off words "An EVACUATION". The full warning and the instruction "be ready to evacuate" fall on page 2, so a reader who sees only page 1 learns neither the hazard nor what to do.
objections.fix: Lead with the hazard and action so both fit within the first 93 characters, then put the source and details after. Example opening: "EVACUATION WARNING (wildfire) from LA County Fire: Be ready to evacuate now. Gather family, pets, supplies." Then add "More info: alertla.org". Drop or shorten the "NEW: This is an emergency message from..." preamble, which uses most of page 1. Recount characters and pages after the edit.
